[quote=the_crystalline_empire;61665703][b]August 9, 2028: Surrender of Belgarde[/b]

Antoine Jacques stood at the window of the ducal palace as he stared out onto the square, where the citizens had gathered to welcome the Sallach Army, which had marched into the city the night before, Lor had fled the day earlier to Mittlemarkke upon hearing word that the soldiers who were travelling to save the city had defected upon crossing the border into Belgarde.

The regime has collapsed, he said aloud to no-one in particular.

Turning away from the window he moved to his desk where he picked up a crumpled piece of paper, it was a surrender speech, he smoothed it out, tapped his cane as he read it, and then walked out onto the balcony overfacing the square where the protestors had gathered.

Citizens of Belgarde, this marks a turning point in Rosenmarkket history, as the old order returns, we must ask ourselves, what next?. It is in this new period that comes upon us like the dawn, that I ask for you to remain loyal to Belgarde, loyal to each-other, and loyal to the nation! Do not allow the government to oppress you, stand up, and act valiantly! Peace! Order! Security! Ariscați-vă, popoare! și luptați pro libertate, pro libertate mare, pro justiție! 

The crowd cheered as Jacques bowed to the crowd, and then left the balcony, moving to the back halls where he would get into a car to meet the leadership of the Sallach armed forces.

[b]Haakons Rage[/b]

Belgarde has fallen, the army has fallen, declared Haakon to Begren, who had been summoned following the surrender of Belgarde.

Sir, I would advise, that you begin negotiations with the secessionists, replied Begren, It has become clear that we cannot, and do not, have the structure to maintain the nation, if we negotiate we can perhaps establish a new government, and reverse course,

I do not negotiate with terrorists, replied Haakon.

The situation is untenable, the officers are leaving en masse, even the loyalists are questioning the leadership, replied Begren.

The loyalists were paid actors, muttered Haakon.

Bergen remained stone-faced as Haakon continued pacing, How can they do this?! demanded Haakon.

They are cowards, failures, traitors! declared Haakon, These leaders, these spies, these are the scum of the Rosenmarkket people! You are the scum with them! he pointed at Begren, You! YOU! YOU! he paused to dab a towel over his head before continuing, They spend years in the academie, and for what? To learn how to write with a ballpoint pen! he continued, Failures, miserable cowards, I shouldve had you all shot! BANG! BANG! BANG! ALL DEAD! he screamed, sitting down once more. 

Begren remained calm, Sir, the situation is untenable, we are best to backpeddle and review our current options, 

NO! NO! NO! I WILL DIE WITH THIS NATION! screamed Haakon.

Very well sir, if you wish to die, then you may, but I shall live, replied Begren cooly, before saluting, and leaving the room.
